entries.title: Jeremiah 8:1
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The bones - This denotes the utter desolation of the city, not only rasing the walls, but turning up the very sepulchres which were accounted sacred, and not to be violated.

entries.title: Jeremiah 8:4
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Not arise - Will they never think of rising again? Not return - Will he wander for ever?

entries.title: Jeremiah 8:5
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Deceit - Their false prophets, encouraging themselves in their wickedness, and pleasing themselves, that their miseries should not come upon them.

entries.title: Jeremiah 8:7
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Appointed time - The seasons of her going and coming. The judgment - God's vengeance, hovering over Jerusalem, and Judea.

entries.title: Jeremiah 8:8
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: How - These things considered where is your wisdom? He speaks to the whole body of the people. The Lord - This may have a more special eye to the priests. In vain - For any use they made of it; neither need it ever have been copied out by the scribe. A scribe was a teacher, one well versed in the scripture, or esteemed to be so.

entries.title: Jeremiah 8:13
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Pass away - Shall be taken away by their enemies.

entries.title: Jeremiah 8:14
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Why - The people at length seem to bethink themselves, and thus to bespeak each other. Silent - Keep close within our walls.

entries.title: Jeremiah 8:16
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The snorting - The fury of the Chaldeans march is described by the snorting of their horses, which is a noise they make through their nostrils. Heard - Even to Jerusalem. Have devoured - It is spoken in a prophetical style, who use to express the certainty of what shall be, as if it actually were already.

entries.title: Jeremiah 8:17
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Shall bite - There will be no appeasing their fury by any method.

entries.title: Jeremiah 8:18
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Sorrow - The prophet now seems to speak, how greatly the calamity of this people affected him.

entries.title: Jeremiah 8:19
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Why - As if God should seem to reply; let them not think it strange, seeing they have turned their backs upon me, and trusted to idols.

entries.title: Jeremiah 8:21
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Am I hurt - The prophet here shews how deeply he is affected with the peoples misery. Black - I am as those that are clad in deep mourning.
